newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair sees competition on home routes.
newsitem.headline: Finnair sees competition on home routes.

text.p: National carrier Finnair chief executive Antti Potila is expecting competition from foreign airlines on domestic routes in Finland, Finnair said in a newsletter on Friday.
An address by Potila at a Finnair staff meeting was printed in the issue of the newsletter dated September 6.
Demand for air transportation was growing all the time and provided good scope for revenue growth, Potila said. But supply was increasing, too, along with further liberalisation.
"We must be prepared to see other carriers on (Finnish) domestic routes," Potila said.
"Our own growth opportunities lie abroad," he added, but did not elaborate.
Higher revenues and lower costs were key to improving profitability. Volume growth was essential even to keep revenue unchanged "because the price level is falling continuously," Potila said.
He repeated the outlook he gave at the August 21 annual general meeting, saying profitability was weakening rapidly, as revenue growth was slow while costs were rising rapidly.
Although it was not easy to turn the profitability trend it was not hopeless either, he said.

"To improve the result we simply need higher revenues and lower costs," Potila said. Pointing out that expansion through increased supply on overseas routes would also raise costs, he said: "The question is where to find profitable growth possibilities."
Finnair's most recent forecast for the financial year to end-March 1997 is that its result will be weaker than last year's 533 million markka.
